facts.text: I am trying to decide on a weathering technique for my current model build.
I am building a Revell 1/48 F-15E Strike Eagle kit.
I am thinking of using a mix of Vallejo Model Air paints and enamel washes to achieve a worn look.
I want tips on how to blend enamel washes with acrylic paints.
I have a few diorama projects in the works.
I am not sure which diorama project to prioritize.
I have a desert diorama project featuring my F-15E Strike Eagle.
I was inspired by photos I saw online of a model show where one of the winners built an amazing desert diorama with a crashed aircraft.
I started working on the desert diorama base using foam board and plaster.
I added static grass and small rocks to create a desert landscape for the diorama.
I haven't touched the desert diorama project in a while.
I started the F-15E project about three weeks ago.
I have been working on the F-15E project in short sessions.
I am really happy with how the F-15E project is coming along.
I have been putting the desert diorama project off for too long.
I want to get back to the project by returning to the initial enthusiasm and energy when I started it.
I will break the project into smaller tasks, set deadlines, and get started again.
I plan to add more details to the landscape, like rocks and cacti.
I want to experiment with new weathering techniques on the aircraft for a more worn, desert-weathered look.
I plan to come up with a narrative or backstory for the diorama to give it more context and interest.

events.text: Started the F-15E project about three weeks ago.
